subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: An Alberti bass is which kind of accompaniment figure?
options: A broken-chord pattern in the left hand of keyboard music
questions.explain: The Alberti bass breaks a chord into a steady low-high-middle-high arpeggiated pattern, common in the Classical era.

questions.q: In the genre of the stage musical, an 'I want' song typically functions to...?
options: Express a principal character's central desire or goal early in the show
Resolve the plot in the finale
questions.explain: The 'I want' song establishes the protagonist's driving desire, usually near the start of a musical.

questions.q: A melodic sequence is best described as which?
options: The inversion of a melodic line
The simultaneous sounding of two melodies
The repetition of a melodic pattern at a different pitch level
A note held against changing harmony
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic (or harmonic) idea successively higher or lower in pitch.

questions.q: In film music, 'underscoring' (or underscore) most accurately means...?
options: A loud climactic fanfare during the titles
The lyrics printed beneath a song
Background music supporting a scene's mood or action, typically not heard by the characters
Music that the on-screen characters can hear (diegetic music)
questions.explain: Underscoring is non-diegetic background music that supports a scene's emotional or dramatic content.

questions.q: The standard twelve-bar blues progression in its basic form follows which sequence of chords (in bars)?
questions.explain: The classic twelve-bar blues uses four bars of I, two of IV returning to I, then V-IV-I across the final four bars.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, a 'raga' is best defined as...?
options: A fixed rhythmic cycle of beats
A melodic framework of notes and characteristic phrases used as the basis for improvisation
The drone instrument that sustains the tonic
questions.explain: A raga is the melodic framework, comprising a set of notes and characteristic phrases, on which improvisation is built.

questions.q: The film-scoring technique 'mickey-mousing' refers to...?
options: Recording the score before filming begins
Improvised jazz played over the closing credits
Using cartoon sound effects in live-action films
Music that closely mirrors and synchronises with on-screen action, beat for beat
questions.explain: Mickey-mousing matches the music precisely to on-screen movement, a hallmark of early animation scoring.

questions.q: The trio sonata of the Baroque is usually performed by how many players?
options: Four (two melody instruments plus continuo of two players)
questions.explain: Despite its name, a trio sonata's three written parts usually require four performers because the continuo bass is realised by a chordal instrument plus a bass instrument.

questions.q: Which jazz style, emerging in the 1940s, is defined by fast tempos, complex chord substitutions and virtuosic improvisation, associated with Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie?
questions.explain: Bebop is the fast, harmonically complex and virtuosic jazz style pioneered by Parker and Gillespie.

questions.q: Modal jazz, exemplified by Miles Davis's 'So What', is distinguished from bebop chiefly by its...?
options: Strict adherence to twelve-bar blues form
Reliance on rapid chord changes every two beats
Use of static modes/scales held over long stretches rather than frequent chord changes
questions.explain: Modal jazz bases improvisation on slow-moving modes held for many bars, freeing soloists from rapid chord changes.

questions.q: In music technology, 'sampling' is best described as...?
options: Taking a portion of an existing sound recording and reusing it within a new piece
Recording in a single continuous take
questions.explain: Sampling reuses a fragment of an existing recording as material within a new track.

questions.q: In music production, 'multitracking' refers to...?
options: Recording different parts onto separate tracks so they can be balanced and edited independently
Playing many instruments live in one take with no overdubs
Compressing a stereo mix into mono
questions.explain: Multitracking records parts on separate tracks, allowing independent editing and mixing.

questions.q: In African drumming traditions, the West African 'djembe' is...?
options: A set of tuned metal gongs
questions.explain: The djembe is a goblet-shaped West African hand drum capable of a wide range of tones.

questions.q: The Latin American 'clave' is best described as...?
options: A characteristic two-bar rhythmic pattern underpinning many Afro-Cuban styles
questions.explain: The clave is a foundational two-bar rhythmic pattern that organises much Afro-Cuban and Latin music.

questions.q: Beethoven's symphonies are generally seen as bridging which two stylistic periods?
questions.explain: Beethoven extended Classical forms toward Romantic expression, bridging the two eras.

questions.q: Gamelan music frequently uses 'interlocking' (kotekan) parts, meaning...?
options: The ensemble plays in strict Western major scales
All players double the same melody an octave apart
Two parts combine, each playing alternate notes, to create a single faster composite line
questions.explain: Interlocking parts dovetail, each playing alternate notes so that together they form one rapid composite line.

questions.q: A 'drone' as a textural device (e.g. in Indian or Celtic music) is...?
options: A sustained note or notes held continuously beneath the melody
questions.explain: A drone is a continuously sustained pitch (or pitches) underpinning the melody.

questions.q: A recitative in Baroque opera primarily serves which function?
options: To advance the plot through speech-like singing
To display vocal virtuosity in an aria
questions.explain: Recitative uses a free, speech-like vocal style to carry the narrative between arias.

questions.q: Which mode results from playing the white notes from D to D?
questions.explain: The Dorian mode runs from D to D on the white notes, with a minor third but a major sixth.

questions.q: A retardation differs from a suspension in which way?
options: It resolves upward by step rather than downward
questions.explain: A retardation is a suspended note that resolves upward by step, whereas a suspension resolves downward.

questions.q: Debussy is most closely associated with which musical movement?
questions.explain: Debussy is the leading figure of musical Impressionism, using whole-tone scales and coloured harmonies.

questions.q: Motown, the Detroit-based label of the 1960s, is associated with which of the following hallmarks?
options: A polished soul-pop sound with the 'Funk Brothers' house band, tambourine back-beats and call-and-response vocals
Free improvisation with no fixed form
questions.explain: Motown produced a slick soul-pop sound built on a house band, back-beat percussion and gospel-derived call-and-response vocals.

questions.q: The studio effect 'reverb' is used to...?
options: Speed up the tempo of a track
Simulate the natural reflections of a sound in a space, adding sense of depth/ambience
Shift the pitch of a vocal up an octave
questions.explain: Reverb recreates the reflections of a physical space, adding depth and ambience to a sound.

questions.q: Mozart's 'The Marriage of Figaro' is an example of which operatic genre?
questions.explain: 'Le nozze di Figaro' is a comic opera (opera buffa) by Mozart.

questions.q: A ritornello in a Baroque concerto is which element?
options: A recurring orchestral refrain returning between solo episodes
questions.explain: Ritornello form alternates a recurring tutti theme (ritornello) with contrasting solo episodes.

questions.q: In ensemble performance, good 'ensemble skills' include all of the following EXCEPT...?
options: Watching for cues and breathing together
Maintaining a shared sense of pulse
Deliberately ignoring the other performers' tempo
Listening and balancing dynamics with other players
questions.explain: Strong ensemble playing depends on listening, balancing and keeping together, not ignoring fellow performers.

questions.q: Free jazz, associated with Ornette Coleman's album 'Free Jazz' and later John Coltrane, is best described as...?
options: Big-band music with written-out arrangements only
A commercial dance style with simple harmonies
Jazz that abandons fixed chord progressions, metre and predetermined structures in favour of collective spontaneity
A return to strict ragtime forms
questions.explain: Free jazz dispenses with fixed harmony, metre and structure, prioritising collective, spontaneous improvisation.

questions.q: The 32-bar 'AABA' song form, common in jazz standards, consists of...?
options: A twelve-bar blues repeated until the soloist stops
Four eight-bar sections where the third (B) provides a contrasting 'bridge'
questions.explain: AABA form has four eight-bar sections, with the B section serving as a contrasting bridge.

questions.q: The 'blue notes' that give the blues scale its characteristic flavour are most typically the flattened third, flattened fifth and flattened...?
questions.explain: The blues scale lowers the third, fifth and seventh degrees, producing the expressive 'blue' inflections.

questions.q: An atonal passage is best characterised by which feature?
options: A clear tonic and dominant relationship
Strict adherence to a major scale
The absence of a tonal centre or key
questions.explain: Atonality avoids any sense of a key or tonal centre, abandoning functional harmony.
